decisions.summary: A bundle per check: make check-bundle FOR=quote-check|record-format|entry-drift keeps only what that check reads; registry entries only in FOR=all; the check briefs dispatch each agent with its own.
decisions.why: The GM: 'I think we should do both of them' - the first of the two is the per-check bundle. Unchanged since the last CLEAR.

decisions.summary: The question-size cap is 20,000 bytes (question + notes), the record's 90th percentile, picked by the session from a labeled measurement; 18 untouched questions over it (labeled, observed 2026-09-26 after the four splits).
decisions.why: The GM delegated the number: 'perhaps you would be able to pick something sensible, and then we can try that out'. The corrected count re-run this round (make question-sizes): 18 questions over 20,000 bytes, matching the plan.

decisions.summary: The cap is enforced on what a change TOUCHES; untouched over-cap questions are split when their pages are worked.
decisions.why: Implied by the GM's own words: 'the maximum size a question should grow to' is a cap on growth, 'if we end up splitting up some of our existing questions' makes splitting existing ones contingent, and 'try that out' frames a trial. Purpose (cut what a check reads) is reached wherever a check runs, since checks run only on worked pages and make quick refuses a touched over-cap question. Unchanged since the last CLEAR.

decisions.summary: cities/government 080 split by hand into 080, 082, 085; bridging sentences reduced to pointers; session 1 then moved 080's hiring finding into 081 (080 at 15,587 bytes after session 1, a labeled one-shot figure).
decisions.why: The GM asked the session to judge splits for lost context. The added clause records a later move, labeled with date and method; 080 and 081 link each other both ways (verified). 080 now measures 16,522 bytes after the check sessions applied their findings - still under the cap and consistent with the figure being stated as after session 1.

decisions.summary: Homesteads 040 and 210, vegetation 150, religion-and-death 200 split by fresh sessions from a split brief reporting what each part relies on from the others; the dispatching session judges each for lost context before it lands.
decisions.why: Carries 'you should look and see whether you think there is important context being lost or if those questions linking to each other is good enough for a human without depriving necessary context from a future reviewer'. Verified this round: every split parent links to each part and each part back (040/043/046, 210/212-218, 150/152/154, 200/202-206); R6 records the judgment, and the one loss it found - six map modals whose Entry still named only the unsplit question, which would have deprived the entry-drift reviewer of the text the modal was written from - was repaired by re-pointing each Entry to the part that holds it. That repair serves the GM's 'future reviewer' clause directly; it is not new scope.

decisions.summary: The one more measured page is cities/government, recorded as R6 against R1-R5, its small size disclosed as noise.
decisions.why: The GM: 'go ahead and do one more round on one more page, and then do another set of measurements'. R6 does that: it adds a per-question-checked row beside per-item (kept for continuity), states the crashed session's missing turns as a labeled estimate rather than smoothing them, and discloses the three-item noise as D14.4 promised. Its four recommendations are proposals for the GM to rule on, as R2-R5's were, not decisions taken.

decisions.summary: T19's exclusion list adds cities/government and its cut point moves to T51.
decisions.why: Nothing dropped; unchanged since the last CLEAR.
